title: Rice, white and wild, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Rice is a grain harvested from the Oryza sativa plant. White rice is milled to remove the husk and germ, while wild rice consists of seeds of aquatic grasses related to the water lily family. Cooking without added fat preserves most nutrients and keeps the dish low‑calorie.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is a staple food for more than half of the world’s population.
Wild rice contains more protein and fiber than regular white rice.
Rice can absorb up to three to four times its weight in water during cooking.
In Japan, rice batter is used to make the savory pancake dish okonomiyaki.
There are over 40,000 rice varieties, each with distinct flavor, aroma, and texture.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides a steady release of energy thanks to its slowly digestible carbs.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When boiled without oil, rice contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Contains magnesium and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals are important for bone health, muscle function, and nerve signaling.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber, especially in wild rice, helps maintain regular bowel movements.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can cause rapid spikes in blood sugar, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Rice from certain regions may contain trace arsenic; rinsing the grains before cooking reduces this risk.

items.title: Lack of fat
items.content: A fat‑free preparation may limit absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins unless paired with healthy fats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve rice as a side dish with vegetables, meat, or fish, or incorporate it into salads, soups, and pilafs. For added flavor, cook it in broth, add herbs, or season with spices. Wild rice pairs well with nuts and dried fruit for a hearty salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice should be cooled quickly and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days, or frozen for longer storage.
